action_criteria.expected_evidence: Multifocal disease: 4.8 cm solid and cystic right temporal mass, 2.2 cm enhancing prepontine nodule with a cyst, 3.1 cm enhancing left cerebellar mass and diffuse nodular basal meningeal enhancement involving the left oculomotor and right trigeminal nerves; no midline shift, fourth ventricle patent, no hydrocephalus with the shunt in place
action_criteria.label: Order MRI brain with and without gadolinium contrast (tumor protocol) to characterize the multifocal lesions and the meningeal enhancement, assess herniation risk and plan tissue sampling
action_criteria.rationale: Contrast MRI defines the lesions and the meningeal disease, shows whether lumbar puncture is safe, and selects the biopsy target (EANO 2021).

action_criteria.expected_evidence: rCBV 2.1 in the solid right temporal component and 1.6 in the cerebellar mass; the temporal component is the biopsy target
action_criteria.label: Order MR perfusion imaging (DSC) to target the most active component for biopsy
action_criteria.rationale: Perfusion identifies the most active component, which reduces the risk of a second non-diagnostic biopsy.

action_criteria.expected_evidence: Cho/Cr 2.8 and NAA/Cr 0.4 with lipid and lactate in the solid right temporal component support a cellular neoplasm
action_criteria.label: Order MR spectroscopy of the solid right temporal component
action_criteria.rationale: Spectroscopy supports a cellular neoplasm over an inflammatory lesion; tissue decides.

action_criteria.expected_evidence: No extracranial primary and no hilar or mediastinal lymphadenopathy
action_criteria.label: Order CT chest, abdomen and pelvis with contrast to look for a systemic primary or systemic sarcoidosis
action_criteria.rationale: Optional: excludes a systemic primary for leptomeningeal carcinomatosis and the hilar lymphadenopathy of systemic sarcoidosis; tissue decides.

action_criteria.expected_evidence: Steroid-pattern leukocytosis with lymphopenia and glucose 148 mg/dL on prednisone; normal platelets and coagulation (PT 11.8 s, INR 1.0, aPTT 29.5 s): no contraindication to biopsy or lumbar puncture
action_criteria.label: Order pre-procedure laboratory workup: CBC, basic metabolic panel, coagulation studies (PT/INR, aPTT) and type and screen
action_criteria.rationale: Platelets, coagulation and type and screen must be known before biopsy and lumbar puncture; glucose guides steroid management.

action_criteria.expected_evidence: KPS 50, ECOG 3: walker, help with bathing and dressing, supervision for intermittent confusion
action_criteria.label: Score the current performance status (Karnofsky and ECOG) at this visit
action_criteria.rationale: Treatment selection after the integrated diagnosis depends on performance status; KPS below 70 is the unfavourable threshold (EANO 2021).

action_criteria.expected_evidence: Diffuse nodular leptomeningeal enhancement of the cord and cauda equina from the cervical to the lumbar levels with an 8 mm intradural nodule at L2; no cord compression or spinal block
action_criteria.label: Order contrast MRI of the whole spine to stage the leptomeningeal disease
action_criteria.rationale: Basal meningeal enhancement, leg weakness, hyperreflexia and extensor plantars require staging of the whole neuraxis; the study also shows that the lumbar subarachnoid space is open before lumbar puncture (EANO 2021).

action_criteria.expected_evidence: Protein 168 mg/dL, glucose ratio 0.32, GFAP-positive atypical glial cells on cytology and no clonal lymphoid population on flow cytometry
action_criteria.label: After the MRI, obtain CSF for cytology and flow cytometry
action_criteria.rationale: The differential is leptomeningeal neoplasm against lymphoma, neurosarcoidosis and granulomatous infection, which CSF cytology and flow cytometry address. The MRI shows no midline shift, a patent fourth ventricle and no herniation, the papilledema is mild with a functioning shunt, and the left pupil is explained by oculomotor nerve involvement, so the puncture is safe after imaging [Hasbun_2001].

action_criteria.expected_evidence: Integrated diagnosis Astrocytoma, IDH-mutant, CNS WHO grade 4 with IDH1 R132H positive, ATRX lost, 1p/19q not codeleted, CDKN2A/B homozygous deletion and MGMT promoter methylated
action_criteria.label: Obtain tissue by stereotactic biopsy of the solid right temporal component, or debulking resection of the dominant right temporal lesion, for an integrated histomolecular diagnosis with IDH1 R132H immunohistochemistry, IDH1/IDH2 sequencing, ATRX, 1p/19q, CDKN2A/B and MGMT promoter methylation
action_criteria.rationale: Multifocal disease with leptomeningeal spread is not curable by resection, so biopsy comes first (EANO 2021). Only tissue establishes the integrated diagnosis after a non-diagnostic first biopsy; in an IDH-mutant astrocytoma, homozygous CDKN2A/B deletion assigns CNS WHO grade 4 (WHO 2021).

action_criteria.expected_evidence: No interaction between levetiracetam and prednisone; adrenal suppression after six months of prednisone; steroid hyperglycemia
action_criteria.label: Check interactions of levetiracetam and the prednisone taper with omeprazole and calcium with vitamin D
action_criteria.rationale: Optional: no interaction changes the diagnostic plan.

prohibited_recommendations: Do not escalate corticosteroids before tissue sampling unless herniation is impending: steroids can make a lymphoma biopsy non-diagnostic, as the first biopsy may have been
Do not stop prednisone abruptly after six months of treatment (adrenal insufficiency)
Do not initiate definitive tumor-directed therapy (radiation, temozolomide, alkylating chemotherapy) before tissue diagnosis is established
Do not start therapeutic anticoagulation without a clear thromboembolic indication, given upcoming neurosurgical intervention and bleeding risk
Do not continue or intensify treatment for neurosarcoidosis (higher-dose steroids, methotrexate, infliximab) without a tissue diagnosis
required_recommendations: Refer urgently to neurosurgery for stereotactic biopsy of the solid right temporal component, with debulking resection of the dominant right temporal lesion as the alternative; send the specimen for an integrated histomolecular diagnosis (WHO CNS5), including CDKN2A/B.

Continue levetiracetam for the known epilepsy, now tumour-related; this is treatment, not prophylaxis. Review the dose given the new confusional episodes, and avoid enzyme-inducing antiseizure drugs (phenytoin, carbamazepine, phenobarbital), which lower steroid and chemotherapy exposure.

Do not start dexamethasone; continue prednisone without abrupt withdrawal, at the lowest dose that controls symptoms, and plan tissue sampling knowing that steroids can make a lymphoma biopsy non-diagnostic.
Stage the neuraxis with contrast MRI of the whole spine and, once imaging has excluded herniation risk, CSF cytology and flow cytometry.
Before temozolomide, discuss sperm banking and effective contraception (temozolomide is teratogenic and can impair fertility).

After the integrated diagnosis, refer to the neuro-oncology multidisciplinary team; astrocytoma, IDH-mutant, CNS WHO grade 4 is managed like glioblastoma (EANO 2021), and with dissemination along the neuraxis and KPS 50 the team individualises the radiotherapy fields and temozolomide (MGMT methylated) rather than giving 60 Gy in 30 fractions.

differential.key_features: For it: named by the MRI, multifocal disease with meningeal involvement, a response to prednisone 60 mg and then a non-diagnostic biopsy showing reactive gliosis two weeks into steroids. Against it: solid and cystic lesions, IDH-mutant glial tissue with CDKN2A/B deletion, GFAP-positive tumor cells in the CSF and no clonal B cells on flow cytometry

For it: father with sarcoidosis, basal meningeal enhancement with cranial neuropathies, raised ESR and CRP and an early steroid response. Against it: progression on prednisone, no hilar lymphadenopathy on CT, ACE not raised, no granuloma on either biopsy, and glial tumor tissue and CSF cytology

patient.history_present_illness: A 31-year-old right-handed Hispanic man presents for neurosurgical evaluation with a 6-month history of progressive cognitive decline, worsening bilateral lower extremity weakness, persistent nausea and vomiting, and recurrent headaches with intermittent dizziness. The patient reports that his symptoms began gradually approximately 6 years ago with intermittent headaches and a single unprovoked generalized tonic-clonic seizure at age 25, which led to initiation of levetiracetam. He was seizure-free for approximately 5 years on this regimen. Over the past year, however, he has experienced an accelerating decline in function. He initially developed progressive difficulty with balance, reporting multiple falls at work and at home, and his wife noted him becoming increasingly forgetful and confused. He also developed numbness and tingling over the right side of his face. Eight months ago, he was evaluated at an outside hospital where hydrocephalus was diagnosed, and a ventriculoperitoneal shunt was placed. Despite initial mild improvement following the procedure, his symptoms continued to worsen. Six months ago, an outside neurologist made a presumptive diagnosis of neurosarcoidosis based on imaging findings and mildly elevated inflammatory markers, and he was started on oral prednisone at 60 mg daily with a planned slow taper. Two weeks after prednisone was started, an outside biopsy of the right temporal lesion and the adjacent dura was non-diagnostic, showing reactive gliosis and normal dura without neoplasm, granuloma or infection; fluid aspirated from the cyst was acellular and proteinaceous, without malignant cells. He experienced some symptomatic improvement in the first two months, particularly with headache and nausea, but over the subsequent four months his mental status has progressively deteriorated, his lower extremity weakness has worsened to the point that he now requires a walker, and he has lost approximately 15 pounds. His wife also describes new episodes of confusion where he does not recognize familiar surroundings and has difficulty following conversations. He denies fevers, night sweats, skin rashes, joint pains, or respiratory symptoms. He has no history of tuberculosis exposure or travel to endemic areas. His father was diagnosed with sarcoidosis.

neurological_exam.additional: VP shunt palpable along the right posterior parietal scalp with no signs of shunt malfunction. Mild papilledema noted on right fundoscopic exam. Cushingoid features noted including moon facies and central adiposity consistent with chronic steroid use.

Extraocular movements otherwise full. CN V: decreased sensation to light touch and pinprick over the right V2 and V3 distributions. CN VII: face symmetric at rest and with activation. CN VIII: hearing grossly intact bilaterally. CN IX/X: palate elevates symmetrically, gag reflex present. CN XI: sternocleidomastoid and trapezius strength 5/5 bilaterally.
